newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX natgas holds technical, weather gains.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX natgas holds technical, weather gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held gains late Thursday in active trade, boosted by forecasts for some warmer weather next week and more technical buying and shortcovering, market sources said.
At 1425 EDT, July was still up 4.9 cents at $2.22 per million British thermal units, while August was 5.3 cents higher at $2.23. Other months were steady to up 5.9 cents.

"We've seen a couple of funds and some shorts buying. We tripped off some healthy stops this morning," said one New York-based futures trader, noting locals used a firmer early cash market to drive the complex higher.

Despite a slightly bearish weekly AGA stock report Wednesday, traders said the recent heat in Texas and the Southwest, coupled with forecasts next week for warmer Midwest and East Coast temperatures, helped trigger some buying.

And chart traders said July's early break of resistance at $2.21 turned the technical picture more positive. They pegged next resistance at $2.25, with a close above that level likely to lead to a test of the $2.36-2.37 area. Support was now at $2.13, then at $2.055 and $2.

In the cash Wednesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed slightly to about $2.20. Midcon pipes were up a couple of cents to the $2.07 area. New York city gate gas was quoted about two cents higher in the mid-to-high $2.40s.
NYMEX said 39,169 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
On KCBT, July was still up seven cents at $2.09, while deferreds were steady to 6.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed 2.1 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
